[RFCS.4.5] **`dsc_hash` is binding whenever a DSC is obtainable.** A
reader that has DSC bytes — whether **embedded** at the front of the
file ([RFCS.13]) or **supplied** alongside it (the replay path,
[RFCS.1.2]) — MUST verify the DSC against its own `dsc_sha256` ([RDSC.3.6])
and compare `dsc_hash`, `capabilities` and `dialect_def_sha256` with the DSC's
[RBND.1.3] tuple, field by field ([RBND.3.1]) via the dialect-binding comparison [RBND.6]; mismatch is
fatal (`DS_ERR_BND_DSC_MISMATCH` or `DS_ERR_BND_DIALECT_MISMATCH`).
Embedded and supplied forms differ only in where the DSC bytes come from, not
in whether they are verified. Two streams are not compared: one whose header
holds neither `dsc_hash` nor `dialect_def_sha256`, which the engine replays
without a binding check ([RBND.2.1]), and a schema-only offline dump with **no**
DSC available at all, which can neither replay nor bind to a program. The dump
relies on the in-stream `SchemaDef` / `Slot` atoms, which remain authoritative
for schema interpretation.
